question:
What is the probability of getting all heads when 3 coins are tossed simultaneously?
(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 i.e. \(\frac{1}{8} \).

Probability of getting a head when one coin is tossed = \(\frac{1}{2} \)
\(\therefore\) Probability of getting all heads when 3 coins are tossed = \( \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3=\frac{1}{8}\)

question:
In tossing three coins at a time, the probability of getting at least one head is:
(MTS 2021 Pre)
solution:

Total out comes = (2)3 = 8
At least one head = 7
At least one head = 8 – 1 (TTT) = 7
\(\therefore \) Probability of getting at least one head = \(\frac{7}{8} \)

question:
Three cards are drawn one after another with replacement from a pack of cards. What is the probability of getting the first card a Jack, the second card a black card, and the third card an even-numbered card?
(CGL 2023 Mains)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. \(\frac{5}{338} \).

Total jack cards = 4
Total black cards = 26
Total even number cards = 5 × 4 = 20 
\(\therefore \)Probability of getting the first card a jack, the second card a black, and the third card an even-numbered card = \(\frac{4}{52}\times\frac{26}{52}\times\frac{20}{52}\) = \( \frac{1}{13}\times\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{5}{13}=\frac{5}{338}\)

question:

question:
What is the probability of selecting a black card or a six-number from a deck of 52 cards?
(CHSL 2023 Mains)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. \(\frac{7}{13}\).

Total black cards = 26

Total 6 number cards = 4

Total cards = 52

Probability of selecting a black card or a six-number = \( \frac{26}{52}+\frac{4}{52}–\frac{2}{52} \) = \(\frac{28}{52}=\frac{7}{13} \)

(2 black cards are common in six-number cards)

question:
A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a queen or a club card?
(CHSL 2021 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. \(\frac{4}{13}\).

Number of Queens = 4

Number of Club cards = 13

But Queen of Clubs is counted in both, so we subtract 1

Probability of getting a queen or a club card = \(\frac{4}{52}+\frac{13}{52}–\frac{1}{52}\) = \(\frac{4+13–1}{52}= \frac{16}{52} =\frac{4}{13}\)

question:
A man is known to speak the truth 5 out of 8 times. He throws a dice and reports that it is a four. Find the probability that it is actually a four.
(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. \(\frac{1}{4}\).

Probability that four occurs = P(E) = \(\frac{1}{6} \)
Probability that four does not occur P\((\bar{E})\) = \(1–\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6}\)
Probability that man reports four and it's actually a four P(N) = \( \frac{5}{8}\)
\(\therefore\) P(\(\bar{N}\)) = \(1–\frac{5}{8}=\frac{3}{8}\)
\(\therefore\)The probability that the number obtained is a four = \(\frac{P\left({E}\right)\times P\left(N\right)}{P\left(E\right)\times P\left(N\right)+P\left(\bar{E}\right)P\left(\bar{N}\right)}\)
= \( \frac{\frac{5}{8}\times\frac{1}{6}}{\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{5}{8}+\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{3}{8}}=\ \frac{\frac{5}{48}}{\frac{5}{48}+\frac{15}{48}}\) = \(\frac{\frac{5}{48}}{\frac{20}{48}}=\frac{1}{4}\)

प्रायिकता है कि चार नहीं आएगा P\((\bar{P})\) = \(1–\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6}\)
प्रायिकता है कि आदमी चार की रिपोर्ट करता है और वास्तव में यह चार है  P(N) =\( \frac{5}{8}\)
\(\therefore\) P(\(\bar{N}\)) = \(1–\frac{5}{8}=\frac{3}{8}\)
\(\therefore\)प्रायिकता है कि प्राप्त संख्या वा स्तव में चार है  
⇒ \(\frac{P\left({E}\right)\times P\left(N\right)}{P\left(E\right)\times P\left(N\right)+P\left(\bar{E}\right)P\left(\bar{N}\right)}\)

= \(\frac{\frac{5}{48}}{\frac{20}{48}}=\frac{1}{4}\)

question: Find the probability of getting a sum of at least 8 while throwing 2 dice if neither of the two dice shows a number less than 4.
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 1/4.

Sample set on throwing two dices = (1, 1) (1, 2)...... (6, 6) = 36

Favourable cases (sum of 8 or more and no dice shows a number less than 4) = (4, 4) (4, 5) (4, 6)(5, 4) (5, 5) (5, 6) (6, 4) (6, 5) (6, 6) = 9

Probability = Number of favourable cases/Total cases

Probability = 9/36 = 1/4
question_hi: 2 पासों को फेंकने पर कम से कम 8 का योग आने की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए, यदि दोनों में से किसी भी पासे पर 4 से कम अंक नहीं आता है।

question:
A bag contains 4 purple, 1 white, and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that none of the balls drawn is blue?
(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution:

Number of ways in which none of the balls drawn are Blue = \(5_{C_2}=\frac{5\times4\times3!}{3!\times2}\) = 10
Total number of ways in which 2 balls can be drawn out of all the 7 balls = \(7_{C2}\) = \(\frac{7\times6\times5!}{{5!\times2!}}\) = 21
\(\therefore\) Probability that none of the balls is blue = \( \frac{10}{21}\)

question: In grade 11 of a school, 40 students opted for Physics, 17 opted for Biology, and 20 opted for Chemistry. If the total number of students in grade 11 was 60, all of these students opted for at least one of the three subjects mentioned here, and exactly five of these students opted for all these three subjects, what is the probability that a randomly selected student of grade 11 of this school would have opted for exactly one of these three subjects?
solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 i.e. 0.80.

Total number of students = 60

Number of students who opted two or more subjects = 40 + 17 + 20 - 60 - 5 = 12

So, the number of students who opted for exactly one subject = 60 - 12 = 48

Required probability = \(\frac{48}{60}\) = 0.80
question_hi: एक स्कूल के 11वीं कक्षा में 40 छात्रों ने भौतिकी, 17 ने जीवविज्ञान और 20 ने रसायन विज्ञान का चयन किया। यदि 11वीं कक्षा में छात्रों की कुल संख्या 60 थी, तो इन सभी छात्रों ने यहाँ बताए गए तीन विषयों में से कम से कम एक विषय चुना, और इनमें से ठीक पाँच छात्रों ने इन तीनों विषयों को चुना, तो इस बात की क्या संभावना है कि इस स्कूल के 11वीं कक्षा के यादृच्छिक रूप स चुने गए छात्र ने इन तीनों विषयों में से ठीक एक विषय चुना होगा।

दो या अधिक विषय चुनने वाले छात्रों की संख्या = 40 + 17 + 20 - 60 - 5 = 12

अतः, केवल एक विषय चुनने वाले छात्रों की संख्या = 60 - 12 = 48

आवश्यक प्रायिकता = \(\frac{48}{60}\) = 0.80

question:

question:

question:
A bag contains 6 red balls and 4 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random. Find the probability that they are of the same color.
(CGL 2023 Mains)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. \(\frac{7}{15}\).

Number of ways in which 2 red balls are selected from 6 red balls =  \(6_{C_2}=\frac{6\times5\times4!}{4!\times2!}=15\)
Number of ways in which 2 blue balls are selected from 4 blue balls =  \(4_{C_2}=\frac{4\times3\times2!}{2!\times2!}=6 \)
Total number of ways in which 2 balls are selected from 10 balls = \(10_{C_2}=\frac{10\times9\times8!}{8!\times2!}=45\)
\(\therefore\) Probability that they are of the same colour = \( \frac{15+6}{45}=\ \frac{21}{45}=\frac{7}{15}\)

question:

question:

solution:

Both are oranges = P(A) = \(\frac{{20}_{C_2}}{{30}_{C_2}}\)
= \(\frac{\frac{20\times19\times18!}{18!\times2}}{435}\) = \(\frac{190}{435}\)

= \(\frac{190}{435}+\frac{231}{435}\) – \( \frac{105}{435}\) = \( \frac{316}{435}\)

question:
A bag contains 2 red, 3 green, and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that none of the balls drawn is blue?
(MTS 2021 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. \(\frac{10}{21}\).

Total number of ways of selecting two balls = \( 7_{C_2}\) = \(\frac{7\times6}{2}\) = 21
Number of ways of selecting 2 balls without getting a blue ball = \(5_{C_2}={\frac{5\times4}{2}=10}\)
\(\therefore \)Required probability = \(\frac{10}{21}\)

question:
If we select 3 persons randomly from a group consisting of 4 men, 3 women, and 2 boys, then the probability that 2 men are selected is:
(MTS 2021 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. ​​\(\frac{5}{14} \).

= \( \left(2\times3\times5\right)\times\frac{\left(3\times2\right)}{\left(9\times8\times7\right)}\)= \(\frac{5}{14} \)

question:
An urn contains 10 black and 5 white balls. Two balls are drawn from the urn one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both drawn balls are black?
(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. \(\frac{3}{7}\).

Probability that both balls are black = \( \frac{{10}_{C_1}}{{15}_{C_1}}\times\frac{9_{C_1}}{{14}_{C_1}}\)
= \(\frac{10}{15}\times\frac{9}{14}=\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{9}{14}\) = \(\frac{3}{7}\)

(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution_hi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 अर्थात \(\frac{3}{7}\) है।

संभावना है कि दोनों गेंदें काली हो = \( \frac{{10}_{C_1}}{{15}_{C_1}}\times\frac{9_{C_1}}{{14}_{C_1}}\)
= \(\frac{10}{15}\times\frac{9}{14}=\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{9}{14}\)= \(\frac{3}{7}\)

question:
A box contains 2 black, 6 green, and 4 yellow balls. If 2 balls are picked up at random, the probability that both are yellow is:
(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 i.e. \(\frac{1}{11}\).

= \(\frac{4\times3}{12\times11}=\frac{1}{11}\)

question:
A bag contains balls numbered 1, 2, 3, ..... 30. One ball is drawn from the bag at random. What is the probability that the number on the ball drawn is divisible by 4 or 6 ?
(MTS 2019 Pre)
solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. \(\frac{1}{3}\).

Number of balls = 30
Number divisible by 4 or 6: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 6, 18, 30 = 10 (total)  
\( \therefore \) Required probability \(=\frac{10}{30}=\frac{1}{3} \)

(MTS 2019 Pre)
